Congress has declared war eleven times, in five conflicts: the War of 1812, the Mexican-American War, the Spanish-American War, and the two world wars. Each declaration was a joint resolution or act signed by the President.

## Key provisions

- A declaration creates a state of war under international and domestic law and authorizes the President to use the whole of the armed forces.
- It automatically activates standby statutes written for 'time of war', covering enemy aliens, trade with the enemy, surveillance, and mobilization.
- The last declarations, against Bulgaria, Hungary, and Romania, were approved on June 5, 1942.

## Why it matters

Since 1942 Congress has authorized force by narrower resolutions such as the [2001 AUMF](aumf-2001.qmd), which do not trigger most wartime statutes. That is why the declared-war requirement in the [Alien Enemies Act](alien-enemies-1798.qmd) and the [Trading with the Enemy Act](twea-1917.qmd) still matters, and why Section 2(c) of the [War Powers Resolution](wpr-1973.qmd) lists a declaration of war first among the grounds for using force.

## Current status

No declaration has been enacted since June 1942. Statutes triggered by a declared war remain on the books and would activate on a new declaration.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [Constitution (war powers)](constitution-war-powers.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [2001 AUMF](aumf-2001.qmd), [Trading with the Enemy Act](twea-1917.qmd), [Alien Enemies Act](alien-enemies-1798.qmd).
- **Era.** Founding and the early republic ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 1: Where the power comes from](../study/units/foundations.qmd) (core reading); [Unit 3: Deciding to use force](../study/units/war-powers.qmd) (further reading).
